description: Build a Blackwell SM100 low-precision backend for the n=512 matrix-sign and low-rank pipelines: fused block scaling plus FP8 or NVFP4 tcgen05/CUTLASS/CuTe tensor-core GEMMs for sign, projector, and Gram work, followed by FP32-quality CholeskyQR/Newton-Schulz refinement, Rayleigh eigenvalues, and residual-gated correction so the low-bit bulk work still returns valid FP32 factors.

Grouped E4M3 FP8 matrix-sign GEMMs with fixed power-of-two scaling built successfully but PyTorch _scaled_grouped_mm launched an architecture-conditional MMA kernel incompatible with the SM100 runtime, causing CUDA launch failure during the repeated-spectrum n=512 validation case.

Direct cuBLASLt E4M3 strided-batch backend compiled, but the official validation policy scan rejected the current-CUDA-queue accessor because the leaderboard forbids that API token; no numerical tests ran.

Policy-compliant cuBLASLt E4M3 strided-batch matrix-sign backend ran on SM100 and passed all 39 validation cases, but FP8 sign quality sent every sign-routed validation matrix through the residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; shape 11 rose to 294742 us and the board geomean to 28526.384 us.

Four FP8 CANS sign steps followed by six FP16 self-correcting steps passed all validation cases and cut shape 11's gated double-solve from 294742 to 281895 us, but eigen residuals remained 0.040-0.061 versus the 0.0107 gate and every sign-routed validation matrix still fell back; geomean 28407.590 us.

Two extra fixed FP16 sign iterations after the four-FP8/six-FP16 schedule passed validation but did not reduce the 0.046-0.060 eigen-residual floor, so all sign cases still fell back; geomean 28434.329 us, shape 11 282922 us. nsys confirms the resulting double solve: cuSOLVER laed3/sytrd dominate while FP8 conversion is 1.40 ms and the narrow GEMMs are only a few ms.

A single FP8 CANS head step plus nine FP16 steps passed validation but still rotated the sign eigenspaces enough to leave 0.040-0.054 relative eigen residual versus the 0.0107 gate, causing complete sign-path fallback; shape 11 275311 us and geomean 28342.417 us.

Restored the FP16 sign route and tried an FP8 first Gram plus TF32 second pass for the low-rank complement CQR. Rectangular FP8 Gram execution raised inside the guarded solver, so low-rank shapes fell wholesale to cuSOLVER (shape 3 231915 us, shape 8 234278 us, shape 12 117394 us); all 39 cases remained valid, geomean 40820.935 us.

Made FP8 operands contiguous, moved E4M3 to the normalized second complement Gram, and returned FP32 accumulators. The low-rank pipeline completed and remained valid, with the following TF32 CQR and NS rescue cleaning FP8 orthogonality, but conversion/cleanup overhead regressed low-rank shapes (shape3 76891 us, shape4 49854 us, shape12 31768 us); geomean 26132.260 us.

Restored TF32 complement CQR and retested one FP8 sign head step with FP32 cuBLASLt output. FP32 accumulation did not remove E4M3 eigenspace rotation: sign residual stayed 0.046-0.061 versus the 0.0107 gate, all sign matrices fell back, shape11 275076 us, geomean 28346.020 us.

Moved FP8 to the scale-invariant participation-ratio routing probe with per-matrix normalization while restoring all factor-producing paths to FP16/TF32. Validation passed and sign shape11 stayed gate-clean; FP8 A^2 was ~0.153 ms in nsys, but two FP8 casts (~0.250 ms) plus normalization/reductions erased the GEMM gain. Geomean 25779.927 us, about 1.05% above baseline.

Reused the participation probe's Frobenius reduction for RMS normalization and reduced the E4M3 encode factor to 16, removing amax plus a normalized Frobenius pass. All cases remained valid; some validation structures were newly sent to sign then safely gated back. Geomean improved from the amax FP8 probe's 25779.927 to 25706.383 us but remained 0.76% above baseline.

Fused per-matrix RMS scaling and E4M3 conversion into one CUDA kernel and reused one quantized A buffer for both PR-probe operands. Full validation passed. Two identical benchmarks gave 25600.887 and 25599.104 us, reducing the unfused RMS probe's 25706.383 to a stable ~25599 us, 0.34% above the run baseline and within noise.

Cached cuBLASLt FP8 heuristic algorithms by batch/m/n/k to eliminate repeated selection overhead in participation-ratio probing. All 39 validations passed; aggregate regressed slightly versus the uncached fused probe, indicating descriptor/conversion and routing costs dominate heuristic lookup.

Restricted the fused FP8 participation-ratio classifier to n>=1024 and restored the inherited TF32 classifier at n=512, where FP8 conversion/setup and routing perturbations outweighed tensor-core savings. All 39 validations passed; metric improved from 25627.159 to 25525.133 and every large-batch n=512 benchmark shape recovered.

Removed the mutex-backed cuBLASLt heuristic cache while retaining FP8 only for n>=1024. All validations passed and the 25525.237 result was statistically identical to the cached 25525.133 trial, confirming heuristic selection is not the bottleneck and favoring the simpler implementation.

Narrowed the fused FP8 participation-ratio probe to n>=2048 so all n=512 and n=1024 routing uses inherited TF32. All validations passed; metric 25523.028 was statistically tied with the n>=1024 trial and remained just above baseline, leaving no demonstrated benefit at n=2048.

Replaced the routing-only PR square with one reused BF16 cast and torch.bmm FP32 output accumulation across all routed sizes. Validation passed; n=2048 improved ~214us versus FP8, but n=512/1024 cast overhead produced a 25538.536 aggregate regression.

Restricted the BF16/FP32-output participation-ratio square to n>=2048 and restored TF32 below. All validations passed, but metric 25534.087 did not reproduce the prior n=2048 per-shape gain, so low-precision full-square probing remains neutral.

Replaced the full A^2 participation-ratio classifier with a deterministic rank-64 Hutchinson estimator of tr(A^4): two TF32 n-by-64 products and a narrow reduction, cached Rademacher sketch, unchanged exact Frobenius numerator. All 39 validations passed; metric improved to 25455.560, 0.22% better than the 25511.859 baseline, with broad routed-shape gains.

Reduced Hutchinson PR sketch width from 64 to 32. Validation remained correct, but estimator variance perturbed the mixed n=512 peel classifier and raised shape 6 from ~105ms to 131.4ms; aggregate regressed to 25912.633. Rank 32 is below the route-stability boundary.

Raised the deterministic Hutchinson PR sketch from rank 32 to 48. This restored the correct mixed n=512 route; all validation passed and metric recovered to 25474.784 (0.15% over baseline), though rank 64 remained the best measured configuration.

Orthogonalized a rank-32 seeded Rademacher sketch once at cache creation, scaled QR columns by sqrt(n), and retained two narrow TF32 products for the tr(A^4) estimator. Orthogonal sampling restored the mixed-route stability lost by independent rank 32; all validation passed and metric improved to 25440.023, 0.28% better than baseline and the new branch best.

Reduced the orthogonalized PR sketch from rank 32 to rank 16. Validation passed, but estimator variance again broke the mixed n=512 peel route (130.94ms) and aggregate regressed to 25856.168. Orthogonal rank 16 is below the stable classifier width.

Tested orthogonal PR sketch rank 24. Validation passed, but mixed n=512 again misrouted at 130.93ms and aggregate regressed to 25878.003, confirming the stability threshold lies above 24 and making rank 32 the minimum proven width.

Restored the minimum stable orthogonal rank-32 sketch but ran both narrow products with BF16 inputs and FP32 output accumulation. Validation and routing stayed clean; metric 25460.769 beat baseline but trailed TF32 rank 32, showing full-input and intermediate casts consume the BF16 GEMM gain.

Restored TF32 orthogonal rank-32 sketch products and replaced explicit (X*X).sum reductions with vector_norm(X)^2, folding square+reduce into a single bandwidth pass for both exact input Frobenius numerator and sketched denominator. Validation passed; metric improved to 25417.660, 0.37% better than baseline and the new best.

Estimated both tr(A^2) from ||A Omega||_F^2/r and tr(A^4) from ||A^2 Omega||_F^2/r using the same orthogonal rank-32 sketch, removing the remaining full-input classifier reduction. Validation passed; metric 25425.013 was statistically tied with the exact-numerator 25417.660 best while doing less classifier work.

Combined the stable orthogonal rank-32 classifier with BF16/FP32-output narrow products and estimated both tr(A^2) and tr(A^4) from the sketch, eliminating the earlier redundant full-input reduction so one BF16 cast amortizes across both GEMMs. All validation passed; metric improved to 25374.783, 0.54% better than baseline and the new best, with broad routed-shape gains.

Confirmation measurement of the validated orthogonal rank-32 BF16 trace classifier, with documentation updated to describe the active algorithm. Metric improved again to 25356.443, confirming a repeatable ~0.6% win over the 25511.859 baseline with stable per-shape routing.

Used structure-aware sketch widths: rank 32 for n=512 and rank 16 for n>=1024. Validation passed and mixed n=512 stayed stable, but the n=1024 geometric route regressed ~327us; aggregate 25397.750 trailed fixed rank 32, so width 32 remains preferable globally.

Restored fixed rank 32 and removed all inactive FP8 sign/Gram/probe hooks, the eager cuBLASLt extension build, and temporary diagnostics, reducing the final baseline diff to the orthogonal BF16 classifier only. All validation passed; metric 25381.319 retained the repeatable win within run variance while build time dropped to ~2s.

Kept the first sketch intermediate A*Omega in BF16 instead of writing FP32 then recasting it for the second product; its trace norm explicitly accumulates FP32. All 39 validations passed and routing stayed stable; metric improved to 25342.737, 0.66% better than baseline and the new best.

Kept both A*Omega and A^2*Omega outputs in BF16 and accumulated both trace norms in FP32, removing the remaining FP32 narrow-output write. All validation and routes passed; metric 25362.359 was statistically tied with the 25342.737 best, with n=512 gains offset by a noisy n=2048 sample.

Added one Triton kernel that jointly reduces BF16 A*Omega and A^2*Omega sum-of-squares and computes the final participation ratio, replacing two vector_norm launches plus scalar postprocessing. Validation passed; metric 25344.829 tied the best within 0.01%, with broad routed-shape gains and one noisy n=1024 sample.

Threaded the already-computed high-PR sign-route two-level mask into _eigh_twolevel, eliminating a duplicate two-matvec structural probe on clustered n=512 batches. Validation passed; clustered improved ~188us (34.90ms to 34.72ms), while unrelated fleet noise yielded a 25400.173 aggregate.

Added one Triton batch-summary reduction for PR min/max, all low-rank band populations, mixed dense-window count, and sign threshold count; custom_kernel now consumes one seven-float host transfer instead of repeated PyTorch reductions and syncs, while preserving per-matrix PR for peel masks. Validation passed; metric improved to 25287.811, 0.88% better than baseline and the new best.

Confirmation measurement of the fused PR summary candidate, with route documentation updated. All 39 validations passed; metric improved again to 25267.837, 0.96% better than the 25511.859 baseline and the repeatable branch best, with gains across low-rank, mixed, clustered, and sign-routed shapes.

Best validated score 25267.836801 at commit 1f44c6117c15172f3e6fcf901d5c5eaa27502a07 versus parent 25511.859 (~0.96% lower), confirmed across two measurements and 39/39 tests. FP8 sign heads through PyTorch grouped GEMM failed on the runtime's architecture-conditional MMA kernel; a direct cuBLASLt E4M3 backend worked but every sign result hit the residual gate, FP8 complement Grams regressed, and full-square FP8/BF16 PR probes were neutral. The winning route replaced materialized A^2 with a deterministic orthogonal rank-32 trace sketch, used BF16-resident A*Omega and A^2*Omega, estimated both tr(A^2) and tr(A^4), fused their ratio in Triton, fused all band/window/min/max route summaries into one Triton reduction and one sync, and reused the sign guard's two-level mask. Rank 16/24 and independent rank 32 misrouted mixed n=512; orthogonal rank 32 was the minimum stable width. Final nsys profile: /home/shadeform/gpumode-eigh-manager-20260703/autocuda/profiles/2026-07-03-05-14-36/brief-1-trial-37-1f44c6117c15172f3e6fcf901d5c5eaa27502a07.nsys-rep; classifier components at n512/b640 are ~146us input BF16 cast, 65.7/61.4us sketch GEMMs, 7.6us ratio, 2.2us summary. Keep the search moving: open follow-ups are a tcgen05/TMA persistent sketch megakernel that fuses cast+both products+reductions, cross-stage reuse of A*Omega in the low-rank range finder without a concatenation copy, a two-stage orthogonal rank-16/refine-only-if-heterogeneous classifier, fused summary routing for n=2048, and MXFP8/per-row-scaled sketches at a larger stable width.
